base_override.reason: The engine's OCF-based conservative OE is customer-balance plumbing, not distributable earnings, and is rejected (FUTU/LPLA/IBKR precedent in this sweep): FY2026 OCF was $7,553,900,000 against net income of $498,700,000, and the filer's own 20-F states the OCF increase 'was primarily due to a 36% increase in our customer accounts balances'; the balance sheet carries 'Funds payable and amounts due to customers' of $30,254.2M at FY2026 ($22,279.9M at FY2025), whose increase alone roughly equals OCF. The same flow corrupts the maintenance definition's ΔNWC term (-$9,215,300,000 in FY2026 in financials_history.csv, printing a $9,714,000,000 maintenance OE). For a payments firm holding safeguarded customer balances, net income is the honest owner's-earnings proxy: SBC is already expensed inside it, and D&A and capex are trivial and roughly offset ($14.4M vs $19.6M in FY2026). Declared under bounded authority (c): every input is a figure printed by this run's engine outputs.
base_override.source: Built exclusively from this run's financials_history.csv (engine-filed USD figures): per-year net-income-based maintenance OE/share = (net income + D&A - min(capex, D&A)) / diluted shares, with the ΔNWC term excluded because for this filer it is the customer-balance flow (see reason): FY2024 ($501,500,000 + $14,300,000 - $13,400,000) / 1,048,900,000 = $0.4790; FY2025 ($550,300,000 + $9,700,000 - $9,700,000) / 1,045,700,000 = $0.5263; FY2026 ($498,700,000 + $14,400,000 - $14,400,000) / 1,029,700,000 = $0.4843; median of the three = $0.4843 (the FY2026 value). The net-income-only series gives the same median ($0.4843).

moat_against: No pricing power by design: cross-border take rate fell 0.64% (Q1 FY2025) to 0.52% (FY2026) to 0.49% (Q2 FY2027) — savings are passed to customers, so volume must outrun price cuts forever

Float-dependent profit: FY2026 net interest income on customer balances was $609M of $2,503M net revenue, against income before tax of $660M — rate cuts or paying customers more (guided) compress earnings directly
Contestability: Revolut, Airwallex, traditional banks and stablecoin rails compete in every corridor; customers multi-home and switching costs are low
Regulatory tail: US national trust bank application denied in July 2026 (reapplying intended); safeguarding/AML compliance is a permanent cost and headline risk across dozens of licences
moat_for: Direct connections to domestic payment systems (Brazil/Japan added FY2026; Malaysia ninth in Q2 FY27) plus a broad global licensing footprint — infrastructure rivals cannot replicate quickly
Structural cost advantage from local netting at scale: cross-border volume $243.5B in FY2026 (+31%), 78% of transfers instant in Q2 FY2027, take rate cut to 0.49% while staying profitable
Wise Platform distribution: 85+ bank/fintech partners (Morgan Stanley, Standard Chartered, Nubank, Google Pay, UniCredit) embed Wise rails inside other institutions
High returns on own equity: ROE 43.0% / 31.7% / 25.9% across FY2024-26 (fundamentals.json) on a debt-light own balance sheet, funding a ~$540M buyback programme
moat_justification: Global cross-border payments network with a structural cost advantage: direct connections to domestic payment systems (Brazil and Japan added in FY2026, Malaysia its ninth in Q2 FY27), a broad licensing footprint (new approvals in South Africa, the UAE and Thailand in FY2026), local netting at scale (cross-border volume $243.5B in FY2026, +31%) and 85+ Wise Platform partners (Morgan Stanley, Standard Chartered, Nubank, Google Pay) let Wise cut its cross-border take rate to 0.49-0.52% and still earn a 26% pre-tax margin in FY2026. Returns on the small own-equity base are high (fundamentals.json ROE: 43.0% FY2024, 31.7% FY2025, 25.9% FY2026); the roic_proxy series is not meaningful here (negative in all three years) because its denominator subtracts $27.8B of cash that is mostly safeguarded customer funds, and no gross-margin series is presented for this filer. Capped at 6: pricing power is deliberately given back (take rate 0.64% in Q1 FY2025 to 0.49% in Q2 FY2027), $609M of FY2026 net revenue was net interest on customer balances against $660M of pre-tax profit (rate-sensitive float earnings, with guidance to pay more interest to customers), Revolut/Airwallex/banks contest every corridor, and US regulators denied its national trust bank application in July 2026 (it intends to reapply). CAP 9.8y.
name: Wise Group plc
one_liner: Global cross-border payments network, moat 6/10 — on a corrected net-income base of $0.48/share (the engine's OCF base capitalizes safeguarded customer balances and prints a fake Tier S) the $10.98 price yields a 12.9% weighted IRR with weighted IV@15% $8.77, so it clears 15% only below ~$8.77; the bear case is Tier D (9.7%), so size to the bear end.
